newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GAYLE GOAL FLOORS HOLDERS MANCHESTER UNITED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GAYLE GOAL FLOORS HOLDERS MANCHESTER UNITED.

text.p: Wimbledon's Marcus Gayle ended Manchester United's hopes of a second successive league and cup double on Tuesday.
His fiercely headed goal from Kenny Cunningham's right wing cross in the 63rd minute earned Wimbledon a 1-0 home win in their F.A Cup fourth round replay.
Arsenal also saw their chances of a double evaporate with a 1-0 home defeat by Leeds in a fourth round tie, while an own goal ended minor league Woking's spirited cup run.
They lost 2-1 to premier league Coventry in a third round replay.

Efan Ekoku (twice) and Oyvind Leonhardsen scorned chances for Wimbledon in the first half and it looked as if the London side would be made to pay for their carelessness when United upped the pace after the break.
But the holders found Neil Sullivan in the Wimbledon goal in inspired form. Just before Gayle's goal he made a brilliant refex save to a close-range header from central defender Gary Pallister.
Sullivan's opposite number Peter Schmeichel appeared to have saved United, cup winners in 1994 and 1996 and beaten finalists in 1995, when he raced up field to hook the ball home following a corner.
But the Wimbledon fans breathed a collective sigh of relief when the goal was ruled out for offside.

Skipper Gary McAllister had a hand in both Coventry goals. His fiercely struck free kick in the 11th minute was scrambled home by Noel Whelan after the ball squirmed away from goalkeeper Laurence Batty.
Plucky Woking equalised through Scott Steele in the 36th minute.

But they had the fight knocked out of them 11 minutes from the end when McAllister's cross from the left found the defence all at sea and Scott Steele headed into his own net after the ball had flicked off the head of another defender.
Arsenal, with a cup pedigree almost on a par with United's, battered away at the Leeds defence in a vain bid to cancel out Rod Wallace's 12th minute goal.

Wallace struck his seventh goal of the season after reacting quickest to a long ball into the box. He stabbed a shot against the foot of the post and then followed up to whip the rebound into the roof of the net.
In the night's other fourth round ties Kevin Davies scored a hat-trick as second division Chesterfield beat runaway first divison leaders Bolton 3-2 away and Wrexham beat Peterborough 4-2.
